name: Benni-Raich-Brücke Arzl im Pitztal
kurzbeschreibung: The Benni Raich Bridge in Arzl: At 94 meters high, Austria's highest pedestrian suspension bridge over the wild Pitzenklamm with bungee jumping and views.
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular Benni Raich Bridge (also known as the Arzl Suspension Bridge) spans the dramatic, rocky chasm of the Pitzenklamm gorge in the municipality of Arzl im Pitztal (Pitztal region / Imst district) at an altitude of approximately 880 meters. Built in 1995 as a pedestrian and infrastructure connection between the hamlets of Arzl and Wald, the daring structure—soaring 94 meters above the rushing Pitze river—ranks as Austria's highest pedestrian suspension bridge. Named after the Pitztal native, double Olympic champion, and World Cup skier Benjamin Raich, the delicate steel-cable construction is among the most sought-after excursion spots and photo motifs in the Tyrolean Oberland.

Design, Vertiginous Views & Bungee Jumping

With an overall span of 137.7 meters and a walkway width of 1.5 meters, the bridge sways gently high above the dramatic ravine. The deck is crafted from non-slip steel grating, offering visitors with a head for heights thrilling downwards views straight onto the churning whitewater of the Pitze and sheer vertical canyon walls. A robust, head-high safety balustrade ensures complete security for visitors of all ages. For thrill-seekers and adrenaline enthusiasts across Europe, the bridge is iconic: from mid-April through late October, an acclaimed alpine adventure center operates one of the Alps' most exhilarating bungee jumping stations here, plunging jumpers into a 94-meter free fall toward the gorge floor. At the bridgehead in Wald, the cozy Bungee Stüberl with its sunny terrace invites guests to watch the jumps over hearty Tyrolean snacks.

Visit & Getting There

The Benni Raich Bridge is open around the clock year-round and is completely free to access for pedestrians, hikers, and cyclists (cleared of snow in winter; tread carefully during frosty conditions). Bungee jumps take place on summer weekends (single jump approx. €95.00, advance booking recommended). Arriving by car: Via the Inntal Autobahn A12 (Imst/Pitztal exit), continue on the B171 into Arzl im Pitztal and follow signs toward the district of Wald; free parking is available directly at the bridgehead in Wald as well as in the center of Arzl. By public transit: Take the train to Imst-Pitztal station, then catch the hourly VVT bus route 4204 directly to the Arzl Abzweigung Wald stop, located a short walk from the bridge.

Tips

The bridge is barrier-free and well suited for all-terrain strollers and wheelchair users with an accompanying person. Combine your bridge walk with a scenic circular hike through the wild Pitzenklamm gorge along the Luis-Trenker-Steig trail, or stroll to the nearby viewing platform at the gorge rim for panoramic vistas stretching far into the Inn Valley.
